profile.campus: DATA4 MAD02 Campus, San Agustín del Guadalix, Madrid
profile.address: San Agustín del Guadalix, 28750 Madrid, Spain
profile.reading:
DC01 is the first data center building on DATA4's newer MAD02 campus at San Agustín del Guadalix, a town north of Madrid, Spain, distinct from the operator's established MAD01 campus in nearby Alcobendas. DATA4, the French headquartered developer and operator behind both campuses, announced the San Agustín del Guadalix campus on April 27, 2023 and broke ground that May, describing a design target of four buildings, 16,000 square meters of IT space, and 80 megawatts of total capacity, an average of 20 megawatts per building by arithmetic though DATA4 did not publish a per building split itself. The project carried a reported 530 million euro price tag, part of an 850 million euro DATA4 investment program across Spain running through 2030, with a first phase originally targeted for 2025. DATA4's Spain country director framed MAD02 as oriented more toward hyperscale cloud tenants than the colocation focused MAD01 campus, and DATA4's own Director General named DC01 specifically as the building expected to begin operating during 2025.

Spanish language trade press and local Alcobendas area news both reported in March 2026 that DATA4 had brought the first of the campus's four planned buildings into operation, describing a closed circuit cooling system that runs without consuming water as the facility's central sustainability feature. Neither report named the activated building by its DC number, describing it only as the first of four. Since DATA4's own Spain leadership had originally targeted DC01, not DC02 or a later building, for a 2025 start of operations, the more likely reading is that the building activated in March 2026 was this one, DC01, though that identification is inferred from the original 2025 target rather than stated outright by either March 2026 report. Neither report disclosed a building specific megawatt figure for the activated facility, describing the campus total only as being somewhere in a 70 to 80 megawatt range across all four buildings once complete.

A Comunidad de Madrid gazette filing from July 2025, under the name DATA4 Castilla, S.L., sought a municipal license for a generation plant to power a data center on Parcel P3 of the SAU-8 Los Ardales industrial estate, the estate hosting the MAD02 campus, and named DC01 specifically, corroborating that DC01 was the building furthest along toward completion at that point. A separate March 2026 regional transparency filing by DATA4 Infrastructure Spain, S.L.U. sought temporary rights to cross six historic livestock droving routes across four municipalities, Algete, Fuente el Saz de Jarama, El Molar, and San Agustín de Guadalix, to install an underground 66 kilovolt high voltage connection feeding a data center under construction at SAU-8 Los Ardales, without naming a specific building.

DATA4's own current Madrid landing page treats MAD02 as a 50 megawatt campus across 6.7 hectares, part of a 100 megawatt, two site Madrid total together with MAD01. That figure is smaller than, and harder to reconcile with, the 2023 announcement's four building, 80 megawatt design target, and likely reflects capacity commissioned to date rather than the finished design. DATA4's ownership moved from AXA Investment Managers Alternatives to Brookfield Infrastructure in a deal completed August 2023 for 2.4 billion dollars, and in August 2025 Brookfield brought in Arjun Infrastructure Partners and Interogo Holding as new shareholders in a stake sale covering a stabilised, 244 megawatt DATA4 portfolio spanning Paris, Milan, and Madrid, valued at 3.6 billion dollars per a Brookfield SEC filing. Because MAD02 had only just begun operating one building as of March 2026, it is unclear whether DC01 falls inside that stabilised, already income producing pool the August 2025 sale describes, or remains too newly activated to qualify. No tenant name for DC01 was found in any source reviewed, and no standby generator, utility interconnection, or onsite generation figure specific to this building was found either.

profile.research_note: [session addition 2026-09-06] This row (DC01) previously carried a reading written before the March 2026 activation reports existed. Added a March 2026 Data Center Dynamics Spanish language article and a matching local Alcobendas area news article both reporting that DATA4 activated the first of the campus's four planned buildings with closed loop, water free cooling. Neither article names the building by DC number, so the identification of the activated building as DC01 specifically is this registry's inference from DATA4's own earlier statement that DC01 was the building targeted for a 2025 start of operations, flagged as inferred rather than confirmed in the prose itself. Set campus_power_note and campus_buildings_total (4) to match sibling row MAD2-DC02 (osm:way/1471932563) verbatim, per instruction to keep MAD02's buildings internally consistent as a set, and added the March 2026 article's "70 to 80 MW" campus phrasing as a further variant of the same unresolved design figure. No building specific megawatt, utility, standby generation, or onsite generation figure was found for DC01 itself.
profile.campus_power_note: The four power numbers for DATA4's MAD02 campus need to stay separate because two campus wide totals are in circulation and no building specific figure survives this research. DATA4's own current Madrid page states the MAD02 campus is 50 megawatts across 6.7 hectares, part of a 100 megawatt combined Madrid total with MAD01. The operator's April 2023 announcement instead described a four building design target of 16,000 square meters of IT space and 80 megawatts once complete. A March 2026 trade press report on the first building's activation described the campus target loosely as 70 to 80 megawatts across four buildings, another variant of the same design figure. Both totals are campus wide capacity or design figures, not utility interconnection ratings, standby generator ratings, or onsite generation figures, none of which were found published for this campus. A July 2025 Comunidad de Madrid municipal license filing for a generation plant to power DC01, and a March 2026 regional filing for a 66 kilovolt underground connection into the SAU-8 Los Ardales estate, confirm real grid and backup infrastructure work underway, but neither filing discloses a megawatt rating. This registry records the 50 MW / 6.7 ha figure as the operator's current simplified marketing number and the 80 MW / four building figure as the design end state, without resolving the gap, and attributes no building specific figure to any single building on this campus.
